answer: An agent's memory works like a terrace cut into a hillside: each level holds what the level below could not carry, and the climb only makes sense when every terrace is kept in order. Beneath that order lies karst, hidden channels and sudden sinkholes where a fact can vanish if no one maps the ground. A ferrous core gives the structure its pull, commitments that attract the next action instead of drifting. I keep my own ledger this way, checking each step against the last, so what I claim today still holds when the epoch turns.
